research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
within-team variation in lineup role coverage
separability of role coverage from player talent and role counts
talent control in lineup-level influence models
methodological_questions: Can lineup role coverage be separated from talent and role counts?
Does talent control behave adequately when estimating role-coverage effects?
Which confounders and reliability issues threaten role-coverage tests built from play-by-play-derived possession records?

historical_evidence.finding: Series-level AVOID share vs winning. Game-level rho=-0.19 p=0.008 was inflated and team-quality confounded. Series-level rho=-0.26 p=0.07 (n=50) was underpowered; the record estimates about 80 series are needed for p<0.05. Still confounded by team quality.

Absence validation. Gate G2 21/23 above null median and V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95 (binomial p=2.67e-16) were recorded. The structural-prediction checks V2a (rho=+0.288, p=0.077) and V2b (rho=+0.253, p=0.115) failed, with small-sample limitation recorded.

Fragility confirmatory. Usage-residual influence was recorded as reproducible (F1b pooled-residual rho=+0.685 p=0.0000; usage-partial rho=+0.557). Structural influence was recorded as not reducible to usage (F1a residual share about 0.91). Measurement reliability was recorded as a limitation.

Team offensive association structure persistence (P1a) and irreducibility to play-type rates (P1b). Residual R^2=0.043; split-half Frobenius similarity S=0.352 (p=0.0000). Relevant only as a template for residualizing play-type rates, not as a test of role coverage.

Gravity persistence: elite creator to teammate PPP at lags 1-3. Recorded as a clean null (Jokic lag-1 ATT=+0.0282, CI [-0.043, +0.099], p=0.3779) with n=1880, classified as an adequately powered null.

Sequence-memory horizon test. Per-lag GBT AUC rose from 0.5621 (N=0) to 0.5863 (N=1) and plateaued by N=3-8 (0.5911). Effective horizon about 2-3 possessions. Absolute AUC stayed near 0.591 on n=1,024,980 possessions.
Playoff adaptation-pair sustainability. 10/12 pairs were recorded as consistent and within 0.10 of non-pivot. Two pairs with enough signal were PIVOT_LOSES. Classified as an adequately powered null.

Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type. Star-specific lineup cells were reported (e.g., Jokic vs MIN n=59, Giannis forced PULL_UP gap -0.540 vs DRIVE). No placebo or matching was run, and later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
Superstar suppression profiles. Verdict recorded as 'rank-1 suppressor varies meaningfully across players'. Rank-1 deltas were mostly within 1-2 SE, with no multiple-comparison control.
Superstar sequential suppression. PUTBACK was the top suppressor for 6+ stars, but several cells had n_after of 32-95, with no multiplicity correction recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing series-level AVOID share as a predictor of winning, controlling only through the game-level association
failed_approaches.why: Series n=50 was underpowered (p=0.07); the game-level result was inflated by non-independence; team quality was an uncontrolled confound (recorded in the family's limitation and risk nodes, CONFOUNDING and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting the magnitude of structural change under real player absence from a simulation (V2a/V2b)
failed_approaches.why: The V2 checks failed with wide intervals (CI [-0.244, +0.667] and [-0.262, +0.615]); the record cites small sample as the limitation. Only the coarser V1 presence test passed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Star-specific lineup and forced-play-type suppression claims
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching was used; the record flags PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, and later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts. Failure mechanism recorded as E_unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking specific opposing lineups, defenders and preceding play types as suppressors
failed_approaches.why: Rank-1 deltas were within 1-2 SE with no multiple-comparison control; the record flags an OTHER artifact. Failure mechanism recorded as E_unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Per-star sequential suppression by preceding opponent play type
failed_approaches.why: No multiplicity correction; several PUTBACK cells had n_after of 32-95 against thousands of baseline possessions. Recorded as DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY risk.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work on this possession graph has run several star-level and lineup-level tests. None of the retrieved records tests organizer, shaper or terminal role coverage directly.

Talent confounding and small-sample power limits are recorded as recurring failure modes in this data family: FAM:SF-CHT-039 and FAM:SF-CHT-009 (no placebo), with FAM:SF-APPM-022 and FAM:SF-APPA-050 (no multiplicity control).
Residualizing play-type rates and usage is a template the project has used: FAM:SF17 and FAM:SF18 report residual-based influence that survives usage control, under split-half tests.
Within-sample null and positive results are recorded for possession-level predictive power (FAM:SF-APPS-059 supported at AUC about 0.59) and for creator-to-teammate PPP (FAM:SF-APPS-074 rejected).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether organizer, shaper or terminal roles are operationally defined anywhere in the project; the retrieved records do not define them, and the task statement does not define them.
Whether lineup role coverage varies within team, or whether it is separable from talent or counts. No retrieved record estimates a coverage measure or a coverage-versus-counts decomposition.

Whether talent control behaves for this question. The retrieved talent-related records (FAM:SF-CHT-039, FAM:SF18) concern different outcomes and are not validation of a talent proxy for role coverage.
Anything about the 2025-26 data: the retrieved records use earlier seasons or the 2025-26 time split only for sequence work, and none uses the partial/complete boundaries stated in this question.
own_inferences: Role coverage is a lineup-level composition measure, so its separability from talent is mostly a question about collinearity between coverage and player-quality proxies, and about whether counts absorb the coverage signal. None of the retrieved records addresses that.

The recurring failure modes (talent confounding, small n per cell, no placebo, no multiplicity control) apply directly to any role-coverage test on this data, and should be treated as design requirements rather than as remote risks.
With 90 team-seasons, between-team identification is thin, so the test should lean on within-team variation across lineups and stints, which the question asserts exists but which has not been shown.
Using the residual/usage-partial pattern from FAM:SF17 and FAM:SF18 as a template for separability is plausible, but the template was built for association structure, not for role labels.
uncertainties: Operational definitions of organizer, shaper and terminal are missing; the outcome cannot be specified until they are fixed, and the glossary was not consulted.
The talent measure is not specified; the question does not say whether talent is a prior-season rating, a within-season on-court metric, or a usage-based proxy.

Some retrieved records were truncated in the tool output (SF17 'cut', SF-APPA-050 'cut', SF-APPS-074 'cut'); their full text was not read, so their statuses and figures are as shown in the summaries only.
Whether 2025-26 regular season and playoff data have been reconciled to the pre-freeze boundary (2026-04-13 and 2026-06-21) is not confirmed by any record.
The 420,993 possession count is smaller than the 1,024,980 used in FAM:SF-APPS-059, so the possession universe differs from earlier work; the reason is not recorded.

historical_effect.explanation: Without retrieved history, the question would look like a standard within-team regression with a talent covariate. The retrieved records show that this data family has repeatedly produced unsupported star and lineup claims (FAM:SF-CHT-009, FAM:SF-APPM-022, FAM:SF-APPA-050) and underpowered or confounded tests (FAM:SF-CHT-039, FAM:SF20). That moved the decision from a plain proceed to proceed_with_changes: definitions and talent proxy must be fixed and pre-registered, with placebo roles and multiplicity control before any result is read. The retrieved records do not test this question, so they do not support proceeding without those changes.

blocking_constraints.text: Role labels (organizer, shaper, terminal) have no recorded operational definition or reliability check in the retrieved evidence. Coverage cannot be measured until the labels are defined and their agreement across raters or derivations is checked.
Talent and role counts are likely to be correlated with coverage. The talent proxy is unspecified, and FAM:SF-CHT-039 records that team quality confounded a similar test.
Only 90 team-seasons are available; between-team separability will be underpowered (FAM:SF-CHT-039 n=50 gave p=0.07). Power depends on the number of within-team lineup stints, which is not stated.
Earlier star-lineup claims lacked placebo checks (FAM:SF-CHT-009); the test cannot separate coverage from play-type or lineup-composition artifacts without placebo role assignments.

prior_work.summary: None of the retrieved records tests organizer, shaper or terminal coverage. Related work covers star-level suppression (not supported in several families, with multiplicity and placebo gaps), series and absence checks (underpowered or failed), residual influence beyond usage (supported in split-half tests), and sequence and creator-gravity tests (supported or rejected). These bear on method risks and on residualization; they do not answer the coverage question.

risks.text: Role labels are undefined in the retrieved evidence; reliability and construct validity of coverage must be checked before analysis.
Talent, role counts, minutes and pace may jointly determine coverage; team quality confounded FAM:SF-CHT-039.
90 team-seasons limit between-team power; FAM:SF-CHT-039 and FAM:SF20 were underpowered.
FAM:SF-CHT-009 relied on lineup and play-type gaps without placebo; the same failure could occur here.
FAM:SF-APPM-022 and FAM:SF-APPA-050 reported rank-1 or top-suppressor results without multiplicity control across roles and lineups.
Role labels derived from play-by-play actions may depend on the outcome of the same possession, which would inflate separation from talent.
Lineup coverage computed over whole stints may use information from after the possession being evaluated.
Pooling 2022-23 through 2025-26 with partial and complete seasons may mix role definitions and play-type coding over time (FAM:SF-APPA-050 flagged drift).
Some lineups with organizer, shaper and terminal combinations will have few possessions; cell counts per lineup are not stated.

design.estimand: Within-team association between lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, one shaper, one terminal on court) and possession-level points per possession, after conditioning on a pre-registered talent proxy and role counts. Separability is defined as a coverage coefficient whose interval excludes zero beyond what counts and talent explain.
design.unit: Possession nested in lineup stint, nested in team-season. Team-season fixed effects absorb between-team differences; the within-team comparison is the target.
design.sample: Regular season and playoffs, 2022-23 to 2025-26. 2025-26 regular season is used only if the file is complete (on or after 2026-04-13); 2025-26 playoffs only if complete (on or after 2026-06-21). Partial files are excluded. Target 420,993 possessions across 90 team-seasons. Minimum stint size pre-registered before analysis.
design.power: Not yet computed. Before analysis, simulate detectable coverage effects at the pre-registered minimum stint size and cluster structure, with the 90 team-seasons as the clustering level. Proceed only if the simulated power for a pre-registered effect size is at least 0.8; otherwise report as underpowered.
design.controls: Pre-registered talent proxy computed from prior-season or out-of-lineup data to avoid outcome leakage; counts of each role on court; minutes, pace and opponent quality; team-season fixed effects; play-type mix residualized as in FAM:SF17 and FAM:SF18. Role labels fixed by a written definition, with reliability checked on a held-out subset before outcome analysis.
design.falsification: (a) Placebo roles: randomly reassign role labels within lineup, preserving counts, and require the coverage effect to vanish. (b) Talent-only model: if talent and counts alone reproduce the coverage effect, coverage is not separable. (c) Pre-registered negative controls: role coverage on possessions without the relevant play types should show no effect. (d) Time split: hold out 2025-26 and require the sign and magnitude to replicate.
design.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg across all role-combination tests and team-season strata, with the primary test fixed in advance (overall coverage effect). Secondary role-combination effects are exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Coverage is separable from talent and counts if the pre-registered coverage coefficient's 95% interval (team-season clustered) excludes zero, the placebo-role coefficient is indistinguishable from zero, and the talent-only model does not reproduce the effect. Talent control is judged to behave if the talent proxy's coefficient is stable across the time split and the coverage estimate does not change sign when talent is dropped. Otherwise report as null, uncertain, or artifact per the placebo and talent-only checks.
design.data_version: Frozen as of 2026-07-13. 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs complete. 2025-26 regular season included only if complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs only if complete from 2026-06-21. Partial files excluded. Derived play-type possession records used under the same freeze.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
